clue.text: Suggested right way for ambitious young man?

definitions.text: Suggested right way for ambitious young man?

parts.note: surface reading: advice on the proper route or method to follow
setter's reading: the famous American advice 'Go west, young man', urging the ambitious to seek fortune on the frontier

explanation.surface: Someone offers career guidance to an eager young go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the nineteenth-century slogan 'Go west, young man', so the 'right way' is a compass direction, not a moral path.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan told ambitious youths to head toward the setting sun, so the recommended direction of travel was toward the sunset.

clue.text: Give a lift to wife married to creep

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to inch is to move slowly, to creep along

explanation.surface: A husband hoists his wife after she wed a sneaky creep.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a hoisting device, and as a verb it means to haul something upward, raising it.

clue.text: Seabird requires total protection (ribbed support)

indicators.note: the second word gives cover to the first, so the bird sits wrapped inside the sum

parts.note: a total is a sum
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A conservation notice says a particular seabird needs complete protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed phrase looks like an aside but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone to which the ribs attach at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Was successful Kentucky candidate unstable?

parts.note: to have won is to have been successful
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: Was the election winner in Kentucky an erratic character?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candidate' only completes the election picture: a candidate who won in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonky is shaky or askew, informally meaning wobbly and not steady.

clue.text: Go round fair for fish appetizer

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over, going round
a mop or mop fair was an English hiring fair, now a funfair, held in some towns

explanation.surface: Someone takes a turn around the fairground in search of a seafood starter.
explanation.walkthrough: A mop fair was a traditional English autumn fair where farm workers were hired; a few towns keep the custom as a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around onion, served as a cold starter.

clue.text: In Polish, indicate a city with an ancient history

indicators.note: the following words are placed in the middle of the word for polish

parts.note: to sand is to polish a surface smooth
to mark is to indicate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Polish speaker points at a city famed for its long past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand in Uzbekistan is one of Central Asia's oldest inhabited cities, a hub of the Silk Road.

clue.text: See 26
Unexpected happenings might be the end of your trousers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: surprising events, as in a turn-up for the books
second meaning: the folded-back cuffs at the bottom of trouser legs

explanation.surface: A surprise could be your trousers giving out.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn-up is British usage for both: a surprising event, and a trouser cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprising developments are 'a turn-up for the books', and cuffs folded at a trouser hem carry the same British name.

clue.text: Pacific place involved with a bee

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spot in the Pacific where a bee is buzzing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific in its adjective sense means inclined toward calm, avoiding conflict.

clue.text: Not without accepted rental adjustment

parts.note: a proposal that is accepted is in

indicators.note: an adjustment alters the arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant has not gone without an agreed change to the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Without can mean outside, so its negation is inside, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Grass stuff going back and forth

indicators.note: going back means read one copy right to left, and forth means read the next one normally

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram; this copy is read going back
the same word read going forth, in normal order

explanation.surface: Cut grass is being carted to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for stuff is used twice, backwards then forwards, giving a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted on sand dunes to bind them.

clue.text: Beach-like setting for hot drink

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the first word surrounds the next

parts.note: a beach is typically sandy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A seaside scene is the place for a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade.

clue.text: Pirate state acquires a Dürer composition

indicators.note: acquiring adds something on, so what follows is joined to the end

parts.note: MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: A buccaneering nation seizes an Albrecht Dürer painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dürer was a German Renaissance artist; his name supplies letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: A marauder roams in search of plunder, as a pirate raids ships.

clue.text: Pads protecting large detective

indicators.note: to protect is to shield all round, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Padding shields a hefty sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is Conan Doyle's famous fictional sleuth.

clue.text: Not for nothing, stopped suffering with love

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Having gone without, someone stopped pining over love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for' looks like a phrase within the sentence but is the definition, meaning against.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is the reverse of being in favour, so it is the contrary of 'for'.

clue.text: Moving in secret to stifle deputy head's shrillness

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the jumbled letters close over the next piece
moving means shifting position, so these letters are shifted around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of deputy

explanation.surface: Covertly acting to silence a shrill-voiced deputy headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridence is a harsh, grating loudness, the quality of a piercing sound.

clue.text: Parking increase — starts to break even, thank heavens

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a raise is an increase

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of break and even

explanation.surface: A car-park owner hikes charges and is relieved to finally break even.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise be is an exclamation of relief or gratitude, like saying thank God.

clue.text: Impressive old city takes on American philosopher

indicators.note: taking on adds something, so the later pieces are joined at the end

parts.note: something epic is grand and impressive
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword staple
US abbreviates United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A grand ancient city hires a philosopher from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American philosopher' reads as one phrase, but the philosopher is Greek and American only gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicurus was the Greek thinker who founded Epicureanism, teaching that pleasure is the highest good.

clue.text: Stopped admitting Republican folded

indicators.note: admitting means letting someone in, so the first word takes in the next

parts.note: to have ceased is to have stopped
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A campaign stopped taking in Republicans and collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folded' suggests failure, as a business folds, but here means bent along a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Creased paper has been pressed into a sharp line, so it has been doubled over.

clue.text: What's been written at great length of wall applications?

definitions.text: What's been written at great length
definitions.note: a singular phrase for a plural answer: lengthy pieces of writing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: long, tedious pieces of writing
second meaning: levelling coats of mortar or plaster spread on a surface

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about long essays on wall coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is both a long rambling text and a smooth layer of cement laid on a floor or wall.

clue.text: Crown belittled by Duke — media frantic!

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The press go wild after a duke disparages the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belittled' reads as insulted, but it marks the definition as a crown made small.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled band or small circlet worn on the head, a lesser crown.

clue.text: Old political party that is not without a centre

indicators.note: lacking its middle, so the central letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long-established party that does have some central core.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, very aged.

clue.text: One on the up as college gets closer

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for college
an ender is something that closes or finishes

explanation.surface: A rising student moves nearer as the college term approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' looks like the comparative of close, nearer, but is read as one who closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rises or climbs is, literally, going upward; in typography it is a letter stroke rising above the line.

clue.text: Officer rejected beer event site

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An officer refused beer at a function.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is the place or setting where something happens.

clue.text: Decline when drinks announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a cat laps, or drinks, its milk

explanation.surface: Someone's standards slip once the drinks are called.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a falling-off in standards or a slip into a worse state.

clue.text: Vehicle-free place in Cumbria? That's just a yarn!

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so that part is taken away

parts.note: Carlisle is the county town of Cumbria in north-west England
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Lake District town banning traffic? That's only a tall story!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a story but is the thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread, used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Sound recorder: "World's ultimate in noise modulation"

indicators.note: modulation varies a signal, so these letters are varied in order
the ultimate letter is the final one of the word

parts.note: the last letter of world
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert for audio gear boasting the world's best noise control.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph, the first machine to capture and play back audio.

clue.text: Disheartened England supporters crowd round for drink

indicators.note: losing the heart means all the middle goes, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the phrase
a press is a crowd or throng
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dejected England fans gather round for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Brash character that's used to stress?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cheeky, forward sort of person
second meaning: thick print used for emphasis

explanation.surface: A pushy person is someone who causes others stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is both a person and a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy print emphasises words, and a brazen person could also be described as a daring sort.

clue.text: After end of the Athens debacle, the man put sword away

indicators.note: coming after means the closing piece is placed last
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the

indicators.note: a debacle is a chaotic collapse, so these letters fall into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: After the Athens fiasco ended, a warrior put his blade back.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheathe is to return a blade into its scabbard.
